item.description: Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term as president, defeating the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in a dramatic comeback. Lula is the first candidate to win a runoff election after losing in the first round, taking victory with 51.79% of the vote to his rival’s 48.21%. His win bucks a regional trend, after the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro had spearheaded a radical populist movement. Sabatini examines how Lula's campaign reinvention, youth mobilisation, and the changing dynamics of Bolsonarismo are reshaping Brazil's political landscape. By embracing social media, mobilising younger voters, and shifting attention from his historical achievements to the economic anxieties of ordinary Brazilians, Lula managed to transform the electoral contest. As Sabatini explains, voters were no longer satisfied with hearing about the past. They wanted an answer to a more… Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: World-famous or local legend? New study investigates global and local forms of collective memory and group identity
item.description: Napoleon Bonaparte and Bernardo O'Higgins: two 19th-century military leaders renowned to this day in their native countries of France and Chile. Yet, while Napoleon's name and exploits are known throughout the world, O'Higgins remains largely obscure outside his homeland. This phenomenon demonstrates the distinction between global and local collective memory—the shared knowledge of the past that shapes group identity—and it is the topic of newly published research from Constructor University's Professor Dr. Mariana Macedo together with Dr. Melanie Oyarzun, Professor Dr. Cristian Candia and… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: "Lula ganó terreno en 97 % de municipios y remontó en 211 ciudades": 'Folha de S.Paulo"
item.description: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva obtuvo la mayoría de votos en 2.875 ciudades de Brasil. Lo que representa un cambio a favor de él en 211 ciudades, que votaron por Bolsonaro en primera vuelta y el domingo cambiaron de parecer. 'Folha de S.Paulo' cuenta que Lula logró reducir la diferencia o aumentar su ventaja sobre su rival en más de 5.000 ciudades, que es casi el 97% de los municipios brasileños. Mina Gerais fue el único estado donde Lula revirtió la votación: 76 ciudades de allí cambiaron su votación a favor del candidato por el Partido de los Trabajadores. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: El cambio climático abre paso a los cultivos tropicales en el sur de Francia
item.description: En el sur de Francia, algunos agricultores están apostando por cultivos tropicales como el banano, la papaya y la pitahaya para adaptarse a los efectos del cambio climático. En el departamento del Var, estas experiencias aún son minoritarias, pero apuntan a una transformación de la agricultura mediterránea: adaptar los cultivos a las nuevas condiciones climáticas. Reportaje de Alexandra Renard y Valérie Dekimpe para France 24. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Lula's re-election brings hope for the Amazon as deforestation drops to record low
item.description: Climate activists in Brazil and beyond are celebrating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory as good news for the Amazon rainforest. Davi Alcolumbre disse que o parlamento tem "papel fundamental na busca de soluções para a população" e que Câmara e Senado ecoam as "demandas, sonhos e angústias" do país.
